teams.name: Cachasol Cartel

nameHistory.name: C u M C back KIDZ!!!

teams.commentary: The Cartel keeps first place, and the committee would describe the win as more trick than treat. Mike D. beat Danny by 6.5, the closest game of the week, on a day Derrick Henry, flagged as his worst pick on draft day, managed about a third of his projection. Javonte Williams and Dak Prescott carried it, but the bench was throwing its own Halloween party: Omar Cooper Jr., picked up this week, scored 20 behind George Pickens, and the Steelers defense from the Frum trade scored 9 in Pittsburgh's win over the Saints while the Texans posted a zero in the lineup. With Terry McLaurin on IR, Pickens is the only real receiver behind Ja'Marr Chase, which makes Cooper the most useful costume in the closet. The Cartel owns the best all-play record in the league, but this one only stuck because Danny left the winning points on his bench.

teams.name: Ammonia Coladas
teams.commentary: Mark once named his team Full Moon Beach Monstars, and the monsters keep coming out on schedule: the top score of the week, a third perfect all-play week this season, and a 29-point beating of Baker. John Legend and Pharrell put out a joint album on Friday, and Mark got his own duet on Sunday, with Tee Higgins out of the flex and Bucky Irving each going for nearly 24. It wasn't spotless: Nico Collins scored 1.6, and Mark started the Patriots, the lowest-projected defense of the week, who went negative after the Bears ran them over on Thursday night. The new kicker, Will Reichard, the same Reichard that Sam rented and returned two weeks ago, kicked 13. With Kyle Monangai and Mike Evans both on IR, the back behind Irving and Josh Jacobs is Kaelon Black at under 4 a game, and a team this hot can afford to treat itself to a running back.

teams.name: Christopher Dootron
teams.commentary: The most-searched Halloween costume in America this year is Buddy the Unicorn, a cheerful horror-movie unicorn with something dark underneath, and Sam is wearing it: 5-2 on the outside, a losing all-play record on the inside. He jumped four spots to third with the seventh-best score of the week, beating Hearn's second-worst, and nobody in the league has had fewer points scored against him. Credit where it's due: Luther Burden III, flagged as his best pick on draft day, went for 21.7, and Sam started the Vikings, the top-projected defense, who led the league with 11. The kicker carousel spun again, Tyler Bass out a week after scoring 17 and Chris Boswell in, and Sam also cut Devaughn Vele, who promptly scored double digits on Hess's bench. Behind Bijan, the backfield is Omarion Hampton at under 4 a game and Samaje Perine, a fresh pickup, which is not a depth chart, it's a séance.

teams.name: DINO NUGGETS

nameHistory.name: The Man the Myth the Legend

teams.commentary: UCF knocked off No. 2 BYU in double overtime on Saturday, and on Sunday the No. 2 team in Fadunkadunk went down too, minus the overtime. Mark beat the Dino Nuggets by 29, Justin Jefferson, flagged as Baker's worst pick on draft day, scored 6.4, and Jameson Williams, flagged as his best, went for 23.6, so August turned out to be the most accurate fortune teller in the building. Baker finally ended the tight end mystery by cutting Hunter Henry, and Harold Fannin Jr. celebrated by scoring double digits on the bench behind Dallas Goedert, a saga that has now haunted three straight weeks. The pickups were sharp, at least: Aaron Rodgers, Danny's castoff, started and scored 13, and the Seahawks defense scored 9, second-best in the league. Rico Dowdle outscored Chuba Hubbard from the bench, which is fine, because Dowdle, at about 5 a game, is the only real backup behind Gibbs and Hubbard.

teams.name: Papas McButt Nuggets

nameHistory.name: Why dont you just call them?

teams.commentary: Jordan is 5-2 with a losing all-play record and the most bench points in the league, which makes the McButt Nuggets a haunted house that keeps passing inspection. This week's ghost was Bo Nix, who scored 26.1 on the bench while Jordan Love started and scored 16.8, at least the third time this season one of Jordan's quarterbacks has done his best work in the dark. It didn't matter, because Jaxon Smith-Njigba went for nearly 27, Rhamondre Stevenson for 20, and the Browns defense, picked up this week, scored 5 in Cleveland's win over the Titans. The Tyler Higbee pickup was less inspired, 2.4 at tight end. With Jeremiyah Love on IR, the backs behind Jonathan Taylor and Stevenson are a bag of candy corn: plenty of pieces, none anybody would choose.

teams.name: Table Shepherds McPie

nameHistory.name: your son rip  on line toot
Fernet and The Music Hall Mack

teams.commentary: The Table Shepherds put up the third-best score of the week, beat Hess by 17.9 and climbed two spots, all with the Chiefs defense going negative in the lineup on Sunday night. Trey McBride went for 22.1, Amon-Ra St. Brown played through a questionable tag and nearly hit 20, and Blake Corum nearly doubled his projection. The kicker saga added a chapter: Daniel Carlson is gone, Tyler Loop is in, and Loop kicked 7, which in this house counts as a treat rather than a trick. Dylan Sampson, the other pickup, scored 9.2 on the bench behind Courtland Sutton's 6 in the flex. Foy has the hardest remaining schedule in the league starting with Mark, and with David Montgomery and Jacory Croskey-Merritt both carrying injury tags, the backs behind Kyren and Corum are the scariest thing on the property.

teams.name: $200 Dolla Holla
teams.commentary: Hearn still owns the second-best all-play record in the league and is now 3-4, and this week he didn't even need the schedule to rob him. He scored 79.3, second-lowest of the week, lost to Sam by 23, and left Caleb Williams' 22 on the bench while Brock Purdy scored 11.9. The Titans fired their head coach before kickoff, and Hearn picked up their defense anyway, started it and got a zero, which is a bit like buying a haunted house because the listing said motivated seller. A.J. Brown and Josh Downs combined for under 10. With Alec Pierce on IR, Deebo Samuel is the receiver behind Brown and Christian Watson, and the Dolla Holla is one more cursed Sunday from needing a trade more than it needs luck.

teams.name: Captain Casper's Low Risk Tacos

nameHistory.name: Coach Matty Ps D In Swishs V

teams.commentary: The Captain Casper name finally makes sense: the Tacos showed up to Sunday as a friendly ghost, pleasant, harmless and completely see-through. Brett scored 83.7, third-lowest of the week, lost to Jordan by 24 and dropped three spots. Aaron Jones played through a questionable tag for 3.1 while RJ Harvey scored 13 and Dameon Pierce 11.3 on the bench, and the Jets, the second-highest projected defense of the week, put up a zero while the Bears, a fresh pickup, scored 3 on the bench. The good news: Saquon Barkley came back with 14.1, and Brett started Kyle Pitts over Travis Kelce and got it right. The bad news is wide receiver, where DeVonta Smith and Mack Hollins are on IR and the next man up, Christian Kirk, projects under a point a game, which is less a depth chart than a ghost story.

teams.name: Quintosss... Amigo?
teams.commentary: Jeff once named his team DuJuan Ressurected, and the Amigos climbed out of the grave in style: the second-best score of the week, a 10-1 all-play, and a 45-point beating of Frum. Tony Pollard scored all three Titans touchdowns in a loss to Cleveland, good for 35 out of Jeff's flex, and Quinshon Judkins nearly doubled his projection. The truly spooky part is that Jeff won by 45 with Patrick Mahomes scoring 6, Harrison Butker 4 and the Ravens defense negative 3. He also picked up Brian Thomas Jr., flagged as Brett A.'s best pick on draft day, and Mark Andrews, Hess's castoff, which suggests Jeff is collecting other people's costumes. The committee leaves him ninth for now, but the second-strongest rest-of-season roster in the league is a monster under somebody's bed, and with Breece Hall questionable and Tank Bigsby on IR, Pollard is the real back behind Judkins and Braelon Allen.

teams.name: Los Desperados Sudados
teams.commentary: Some houses are just haunted. Danny scored the sixth-best total of the week, lost by 6.5 to the first-place team, and the ghost in the walls was Emanuel Wilson again: 18 points on the bench behind Matthew Golden's 6.9 in the flex, the only bench decision in the league that flipped a result, three weeks after Wilson scored 25.5 on the same bench. The Brewers won Game 1 of the World Series 3-2, the kind of one-run game Danny would have lost with the winning run left on deck. Joe Burrow and CeeDee Lamb did their jobs, but Dominic Zvada kicked 2, DeMario Douglas, picked up this week, started for under 4 while Rome Odunze more than doubled him on the bench, and Aaron Rodgers, cut this week, scored 13 for Baker. Danny is 1-6 with a winning all-play record and the worst luck number in the league, and at this point he doesn't need a waiver claim, he needs an exorcist.

teams.name: For Heaven Sakes, Woman
teams.commentary: Hess finally started Tre Tucker a week after Tucker scored 24 on his bench, and Tucker delivered nearly 19, which would be a lovely redemption story if the bench hadn't immediately found a new ghost. KC Concepcion scored 19.2 on the bench while Jalen Coker managed 1.4 in the flex, and Hess lost to Foy by 17.9, so the bench bomb came up a tenth of a point short of flipping the game. Devaughn Vele, picked up after Sam cut him, added double digits on the bench for good measure. The rest of the waiver haul was a mixed bag of candy: the Bengals defense scored 8, third-best in the league, and Ryan Fitzgerald, the latest kicker, scored 1. Hess kept nobody, has the fewest points in the league, and now has more startable receivers than running backs, so Concepcion or Vele should be on the market for anything that runs between the tackles.

teams.name: Dad Bellies Doin' Salt Smellies

nameHistory.name: Lots of ??? But Tons of Upside!
Poopy Wake Up Call On Line Toot
The Best Butt of the Bunch

teams.commentary: Clayface, a body-horror movie about a man whose face gets ruined, topped the box office this weekend, and Frum's lineup supplied the live-action version: 68.5 points, the second-lowest score of the season, an 0-11 all-play and a 45-point loss to Jeff. Frum once named his team The Papa Perkensteins, and the roster is now a monster stitched together from Mike D.'s spare parts: Cam Skattebo scored 18.6 on the bench while Kenneth Walker, the $39 keeper, managed 7.7, and Alvin Kamara outscored Walker from the bench too. Bryce Young barely registered, the Panthers defense went negative 3, and Juwan Johnson, another trade arrival, scored about a point at tight end. Zay Flowers, at nearly 24, was the only starter wearing a costume worth complimenting. Frum gets Danny next in the 1-6 bowl, a matchup so cursed the committee is bringing garlic.

commentary.intro: Halloween is Saturday, and Fadunkadunk opened its haunted house a week early. The benches were possessed: Danny lost by 6.5 with Emanuel Wilson's 18 groaning behind the walls, Hess's bench bomb came up a tenth of a point short of flipping his game, and Frum posted 68.5, the second-lowest score of the season and an 0-11 week in the all-play. Up top, the committee has a four-way pileup at 5-2, and Mike D. keeps first even though it took Danny's bench to get him there. Mark posted the top score of the week and his third perfect all-play week of the season, and nobody climbed faster than Sam, who jumped four spots to third with the seventh-best score, because nobody in this league ever seems to score against him. Jeff rose from the grave with a 45-point win, and the reigning champ fell three spots on a day his best running backs haunted his bench.

awards.benchBomb: Hess benched KC Concepcion's 19.2 for Jalen Coker's 1.4 and lost by 17.9, so the bench bomb came up one-tenth of a point short of flipping the game. Devaughn Vele scored double digits on the same bench. That's not a bench, it's a haunted attic.
awards.toughestLoss: Danny scored the sixth-best total of the week and lost by 6.5 to the first-place team with Emanuel Wilson's 18 on the bench behind Matthew Golden's 6.9, the only bench call of the week that flipped a result. Wilson has now haunted that bench twice this season.
awards.lowScore: Frum scored 68.5, the second-lowest total of the season, lost to all eleven teams in the all-play, and still had Cam Skattebo's 18.6 sitting on the bench. The Bellies didn't dress up for Halloween; they came as a forfeit.
awards.highScore: Mark, 122.8, his third perfect 11-0 all-play week of the season.
awards.boom: Tony Pollard scored all three Titans touchdowns the week Tennessee fired its coach, good for 35 out of Jeff's flex on a projection under 13.
awards.blowout: Jeff over Frum by 45.2, and Jeff did it with a negative defense and 6 points from Patrick Mahomes.
awards.bust: Nico Collins, projected for 14, scored 1.6 for Mark, who won by 29 anyway.
awards.worstDefense: Frum's Panthers went for negative 3, tied with Jeff's Ravens for the worst defensive score of the week.
awards.bestDefense: Sam's Vikings, the top-projected defense of the week, led everyone with 11, and Sam actually had them in the lineup.
awards.luckiestWin: Sam won with the seventh-best score of the week because Hearn brought the second-worst.
awards.closest: Mike D. over Danny by 6.5, the tightest game of the week, with Danny's winning lineup sitting on Danny's bench.

commentary.outro:
Halloween weekend headliner: Mike D. against Sam, first against third, the best all-play record in the league against the luckiest 5-2 team in it. Mark gets Foy, the week's top score against the league's hardest remaining schedule, and Baker and Jordan meet in a fourth-versus-fifth game where both benches are scarier than the starters. Hearn gets Jeff, Brett A. gets Hess, and Danny and Frum meet in the 1-6 bowl. SNL is back with its Halloween episode on Saturday, and nobody in this league needs a costume; the lineups are frightening enough.

Trade Desk: running backs are still the currency, and this week the haunted benches showed who has spares. Frum has Cam Skattebo and Alvin Kamara both outscoring his starter from the bench, and Danny has Emanuel Wilson, who keeps scoring wherever Danny doesn't put him. The buyers are lined up: Sam has Omarion Hampton and a fresh pickup behind Bijan, Mark is down Kyle Monangai, Foy's backups carry injury tags, and Jordan's depth behind Taylor and Stevenson is candy corn. Frum needs receivers as badly as anyone, so Skattebo to Sam for Jordan Addison, who scored 3.3 in Sam's flex, gives both teams a starter. Hess has spare receivers in Concepcion and Vele and nothing behind McCaffrey and TreVeyon Henderson, while Danny has backs to spare and just started DeMario Douglas at receiver, so Wilson for Concepcion is the cleanest fit on the board. Move of the week: Baker picking up Aaron Rodgers after Danny cut him and starting him for 13. Anti-move of the week: Hearn picking up the Titans defense the week Tennessee fired its coach, starting it, and getting a zero.

Swish Watch: the reigning champ is 4-3 and eighth, down three spots after the third-lowest score of the week. The friendly ghost has a genuine wide receiver problem, with DeVonta Smith and Mack Hollins on IR and nobody behind Chris Olave and Keenan Allen worth starting, and a backfield where RJ Harvey and Dameon Pierce keep scoring from the bench, so the Tacos are holding exactly the trade bait to fix it. Luck Index, briefly: Sam and Jordan are both 5-2 with 35-42 all-play records, tied for the luckiest teams in the league, while Danny, 1-6 with a 40-37 all-play, is still the unluckiest by a wide margin. Keeper Corner returns next week. Rankings and commentary refresh every Tuesday morning once ESPN finalizes the week.
